executive_brief: This project is a CLI-based To-Do List Manager implemented in Python. It utilizes a JSON-based local storage pattern to manage task persistence. The architecture follows a tiered approach separating CLI command dispatch, service-layer business logic, and a data-access layer for file I/O, designed for incremental delivery from an MVP (Add/Complete) to full task lifecycle management.

architectural_constraints: Strict execution sequence: Phase 1 (Setup) -> Phase 2 (Foundational) -> User Stories -> Phase 6 (Polish)
Data persistence must use JSON format in `~/.todos.json`
Sequential ID assignment for task creation
Mandatory `created_at` population for all task entities
Required `--json` output flag for machine-readable task listing
Storage writes must persist removals and clears safely

maturity_assessment: The project is READY for execution. The specification is highly granular and structured, with a perfect completeness score. While there are minor gaps regarding formal acceptance criteria and performance bounds for the JSON storage, these do not impede implementation given the provided independent test cases for each user story.
critical_dependencies: Sequential dependency: User stories (US1, US2, US3) strictly depend on the completion of the Foundational phase (T004-T008)
File system access for `~/.todos.json` storage resolution
Internal data integrity: Task ID mapping and serialization helpers in `models.py` are required by all service-layer operations
Verification gate: Manual smoke tests of the full command suite (`add`, `list`, `complete`, `remove`, `clear`) prior to final polish
